description: Add independent Proton profiler integration to nano-vllm submodule for kernel-level GPU profiling and side-by-side comparison with vLLM
instructions: All changes go inside the submodules/nano-vllm/ directory — do NOT modify vLLM code
Make clear and simple code design for ease of understanding
Write docstring and inline comments for every method
Write comprehensive tests for every function: unit tests, integration tests, smoke tests
Only write absolutely necessary code, avoid redundant code, keep codebase clean
Avoid fallbacks and try-catch — fail early to discover issues at the shallow surface
Python environment is managed by uv. Run `. .venv/bin/activate` and use `uv pip install ...`
Do not include claude as co-author in commit message
Do not include US-00X in commit message, follow vLLM commit message style
nano-vllm profiler is fully independent — no vLLM imports or dependencies
Use module-level singleton pattern (get_profiler/set_profiler) for global profiler access
When profiler is not active, annotations must be no-ops with zero overhead

userStories.title: Proton profiler module with basic start/stop lifecycle
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a self-contained Proton profiler module in nano-vllm so that I can start/stop profiling sessions and collect GPU traces.
acceptanceCriteria: New file nanovllm/profiler.py with a ProtonProfiler class
ProtonProfiler supports start(), stop(), shutdown(), get_status() methods
Lazy import of triton.profiler — fails clearly if Proton is unavailable
Configurable output directory, context (shadow/python), data format (tree/trace), backend (cupti/roctracer/instrumentation/auto), hook (triton/None), and mode (including periodic_flushing)
Rank-aware output file naming (proton_rank{N}.hatchet or .chrome_trace)
Module-level get_profiler() and set_profiler() singleton functions
A proton_scope() context manager helper that is a no-op when profiler is None
Unit tests for initialization, start/stop lifecycle, config validation, and singleton access
Tests pass

userStories.title: Periodic flushing and phase tracking
userStories.description: As a developer, I want periodic flushing support so that I can profile multiple intervals in a single session without unbounded memory growth.
acceptanceCriteria: When mode starts with periodic_flushing, session persists across start/stop cycles
First start() creates session via proton.start(), subsequent calls use proton.activate()
stop() calls proton.deactivate(flushing=True) and advances phase via proton.data.advance_phase()
shutdown() calls proton.finalize() to close the persistent session
get_status() returns current phase number, output directory, and list of output files
Per-phase output files: proton_rank{N}.part_{phase}.hatchet
Unit tests for multi-cycle periodic flushing sequences and phase tracking
Tests pass

userStories.title: CLI integration for bench.py
userStories.description: As a developer, I want CLI flags on bench.py so that I can run profiled benchmarks from the command line.
acceptanceCriteria: --profiler proton flag enables Proton profiling for the benchmark run
--proton-dir <path> sets the output directory (required when --profiler proton)
--proton-context {shadow,python} sets context mode (default: shadow)
--proton-data {tree,trace} sets output format (default: tree)
--proton-backend {cupti,roctracer,instrumentation} sets GPU backend (default: auto)
--proton-mode <string> sets mode (e.g., periodic_flushing)
--proton-hook {triton} sets kernel hook (default: None)
Profiler starts before inference, stops after, and prints output file paths on completion
Smoke test: python bench.py --profiler proton --proton-dir /tmp/proton_out runs without error
Tests pass
